paragraphs: The paper studies how a visual system can learn representations that make future images easier to predict. Movement by an observer and by objects creates regular patterns across video frames. The proposed self-supervised framework learns from those patterns by training to predict the next frame, making temporal prediction the objective that shapes its representation.

Its polar architecture is motivated by the Fourier shift theorem and a generalization involving transformation groups. The central idea is to represent visual changes in a form that supports prediction. Controlled experiments show that the approach can discover representations of simple transformation groups present in the data.

On natural videos, the framework predicts better than traditional motion compensation and performs competitively with conventional deep networks while retaining speed and interpretability. Its computations can also be reorganized into components resembling models of simple and direction-selective complex cells in primate V1. This resemblance offers a principled framework for studying biological prediction, rather than establishing that the brain implements this particular model.
neurips-2023-a-polar-prediction-model-fo.tldr: A self-supervised polar architecture learns visual transformations through next-frame prediction, combining competitive performance with interpretable computations resembling visual cortical models.

paragraphs: Weakly supervised 3D segmentation learns to label points with only sparse human annotations. Models often create pseudo-labels for the remaining points, then keep only those meeting a confidence threshold. The authors hypothesize that noisy pseudo-labels explain this selective use: disagreement between those labels and model predictions can disrupt training.

ERDA addresses the disagreement directly through entropy regularization and distribution alignment. Instead of relying on selection to decide which unlabeled points are useful, it regularizes generated labels and brings their distributions closer to the segmentation model's predictions. When alignment is expressed using KL distance, the objective simplifies to a cross-entropy-based loss that trains both the pseudo-label generator and segmentation network together.

Experiments across baselines and large datasets show that ERDA can use all unlabeled points effectively and achieves state-of-the-art results in the evaluated settings. The paper also reports that it can exceed fully supervised baselines with only 1% of true annotations. This is an empirical result for the studied comparisons, illustrating how improving pseudo-label training can make sparse supervision unusually effective.
neurips-2023-all-points-matter-entropy-r.tldr: ERDA jointly regularizes pseudo-labels and aligns predictions, enabling effective use of all unlabeled points for 3D segmentation with sparse annotations.

paragraphs: Recovering an image from measurements becomes harder when the measurement process is itself unknown. Such blind inverse problems require estimating both the image and the operator that produced the observations. Existing plug-and-play methods combine physical measurement models with learned denoisers, but their use has largely focused on cases where the measurement operator is known.

The proposed block-coordinate plug-and-play method extends this approach by placing learned denoiser priors on both unknown quantities. This makes denoising part of the joint estimation process for images and measurement operators. The accompanying theory accommodates nonconvex data-fitting objectives and expansive denoisers, broadening the mathematical setting considered for this blind reconstruction problem.

The convergence analysis concerns a stationary point of an implicit function associated with an approximate minimum mean-squared error denoiser; it does not claim recovery of a global optimum. Numerical studies cover automatic MRI coil sensitivity estimation and blind image deblurring. Together, the analysis and experiments support an efficient, principled way to apply learned denoisers when uncertainty extends to the measurement process itself.
neurips-2023-block-coordinate-plug-and-p.tldr: BC-PnP uses learned denoisers to jointly estimate images and unknown measurement operators, with convergence analysis and validation on two blind imaging problems.

paragraphs: Differential privacy is commonly interpreted as protection against determining whether a particular example appeared in training. Reconstructing an entire training example is a different, more ambitious attack. This paper examines how to measure protection against reconstruction specifically for DP-SGD, motivated by evidence that this narrower protection objective may require less noise and allow more useful models.

The authors derive an upper bound on the success of any reconstruction attack against DP-SGD. They also construct an attack whose empirical results match the bound's predictions. These complementary contributions connect a theoretical limit on attack success with observed attack behavior, supporting more detailed investigation of how training parameters affect reconstruction protection.

A key finding is that DP-SGD parameter settings with the same differential privacy guarantees can have substantially different reconstruction success rates. Thus, the privacy guarantee alone may be an inadequate proxy for this particular threat. The results provide tools for studying reconstruction-focused parameter choices, while preserving the distinction between protecting against reconstruction and protecting against membership inference.
neurips-2023-bounding-training-data-reco.tldr: A reconstruction-success bound and matching empirical attack show that identical DP guarantees can conceal substantial differences in DP-SGD reconstruction protection.

paragraphs: Recommendation systems must decide how often to contact users as well as which messages to send. This paper models a setting where messages from a selected list arrive periodically and feedback is randomly delayed. If a user dislikes a message, they may leave, with abandonment probability increasing with recommendation frequency. Different messages can also deliver different rewards.

The learning problem therefore involves discovering both message appeal and users' abandonment behavior. The authors first give a dynamic programming solution for finding an optimal message sequence in deterministic scenarios. They then develop a polynomial-time offline learning algorithm based on upper confidence bounds and characterize its performance through a regret bound.

For the online setting, the paper introduces an algorithm that can adapt content for an individual user. Numerical experiments on the AmEx dataset support the algorithms' effectiveness. The contribution is a recommendation framework that explicitly accounts for the interaction between timing, delayed observations, message value, and abandonment, rather than treating every successful recommendation as equally rewarding.
neurips-2023-cascading-bandits-optimizin.tldr: The paper develops recommendation algorithms that account for sending frequency, delayed feedback, unequal message rewards, and users' risk of abandoning the system.

paragraphs: Secure two-party computation can protect privacy during neural network inference, but the communication it requires can cause substantial latency. Earlier optimization methods often use the number of ReLU operations as a stand-in for communication cost. The authors find that this misses much of the cost in modern protocols, where other linear and nonlinear operations account for the majority of communication.

CoPriv jointly changes the inference protocol and network architecture. It introduces a convolution protocol based on the Winograd transformation, incorporates optimizations informed by the network, and develops network optimization compatible with that protocol. This coordinated approach targets communication across linear and nonlinear operations instead of concentrating on one operation type.

Against CrypTFlow2, CoPriv reports a 2.1-fold communication reduction for ResNet-18 and ResNet-32 on CIFAR-100. Compared with SNL, it reports 9.98-fold lower online communication and 3.88-fold lower total communication with higher accuracy. Against MetaPruning, it reports 3.87-fold lower online communication and over 3% higher accuracy. These comparisons support optimizing the network and secure protocol together.
neurips-2023-copriv-network-protocol-co-.tldr: CoPriv jointly optimizes neural networks and secure computation protocols to reduce private-inference communication across linear and nonlinear operations.

paragraphs: This paper studies how to select a diverse summary while satisfying prescribed representation requirements. Data points belong to groups, and the summary must contain a specified number from each group. Diversity is measured either by adding all pairwise distances among selected points or by adding each selected point's distance to its nearest selected neighbor.

The authors construct core-sets: smaller collections that support the constrained selection problem. For pairwise-distance diversity, they provide the first constant-factor core-set whose size does not depend on dataset size or aspect ratio. For nearest-neighbor diversity, they provide the first core-set result. These guarantees address how much data must be retained to support diverse selection under group quotas.

Experiments include summarizing timed messages with quotas that favor recent messages. In this application, the core-set method achieves a 100-fold speedup while reducing diversity by only a few percent. The approach also improves space usage in a streaming setting. These results show how a mathematical summary of the selection problem can make a practical summarization task substantially cheaper.
neurips-2023-core-sets-for-fair-and-dive.tldr: New core-sets accelerate diverse subset selection under group quotas, including a message-summary application with a 100-fold speedup and a small diversity loss.

paragraphs: Curriculum reinforcement learning helps an agent approach a difficult goal through intermediate tasks. Choosing those tasks becomes challenging when observations are high-dimensional, so previous methods often depend on manually defined goal spaces. CQM instead learns a semantic goal space automatically and uses it to propose intermediate goals that guide progress toward the final objectives.

The method uses a vector-quantized variational autoencoder to turn continuous observations into discrete representations. It then builds a graph to recover temporal relationships between those representations. Together, the discrete states and their temporal connections provide a structured space for choosing goals. Goal selection considers both uncertainty and temporal distance.

The authors demonstrate efficient exploration in an initially uninformed environment using only raw examples of the desired goals. Across several goal-reaching tasks, CQM exceeds state-of-the-art curriculum methods in data efficiency and performance, including tasks with first-person visual inputs. These results support learning the space in which a curriculum operates, alongside selecting the curriculum itself, as a way to handle complex observations.
neurips-2023-cqm-curriculum-reinforcemen.tldr: CQM learns a discrete, temporally connected goal space and selects uncertainty-aware intermediate goals to improve curriculum reinforcement learning.

paragraphs: The paper studies how a pretrained model for one modality can teach representations to a model for another modality using paired data. The resulting model is intended to support tasks in a zero-shot setting. Conventional contrastive training organizes examples into positive and negative relationships, even though real similarities between examples can vary by degree.

Continuously Weighted Contrastive Loss replaces this binary treatment with a continuous similarity measure. Its aim is to transfer the structure of the pretrained model's embedding space across modalities. This matters because relationships among training examples contain information beyond whether a particular pair is designated a match: some examples are more similar than others.

The authors report improved zero-shot transfer across multiple models, datasets, and modalities using publicly available data. Reported gains over previous state-of-the-art methods are 5–8 percentage points for image classification and 20–30 percentage points for speech-to-intent and keyword classification. These results support the usefulness of graded similarity for cross-modal representation transfer in the evaluated settings.
neurips-2023-cwcl-cross-modal-transfer-w.tldr: CWCL transfers representations across modalities using continuous similarity weights, improving zero-shot image and speech classification in the reported evaluations.

paragraphs: Explaining a graph neural network involves identifying graph structures that strongly influence its predictions. The paper argues that an explanation should also resemble graphs from the relevant data distribution. Otherwise, the network's sensitivity to unfamiliar inputs can undermine the explanation. Methods constrained to structures within the original graph may give insufficient attention to this distributional requirement.

D4Explainer incorporates generative learning of graph distributions into its explanation objective using discrete denoising diffusion. It addresses two explanation tasks within one framework. For an individual example, it generates diverse counterfactual graphs that conform to the data distribution. At the model level, it identifies graph patterns that are especially informative for a particular predicted class.

Evaluations on synthetic and real-world datasets report state-of-the-art performance in explanation accuracy, faithfulness, diversity, and robustness. The central contribution is connecting explanations to a learned distribution of plausible graphs while supporting both individual and class-level analysis. This makes distributional plausibility an explicit part of the explanation process rather than relying solely on structural changes to an input.
neurips-2023-d4explainer-in-distribution.tldr: D4Explainer learns graph distributions to generate plausible counterfactual and model-level GNN explanations within a unified diffusion-based framework.

paragraphs: Conditional stochastic optimization includes problems arising in portfolio selection, reinforcement learning, robust learning, and causal inference. Its nested structure creates a specific obstacle: averaging sampled gradients produces a biased estimate of the objective's gradient. That systematic error can make convergence require many samples, even when sampling is used to make each update manageable.

The paper introduces a general stochastic extrapolation technique that reduces this bias. For smooth, nonconvex objectives, the authors combine extrapolation with variance reduction and establish substantially improved sample-complexity bounds. The combination addresses both systematic estimation error and variability in stochastic estimates, allowing stronger convergence results than the existing bounds considered.

The authors also develop algorithms for the finite-sum version of conditional stochastic optimization and improve the corresponding theoretical results. The contribution is therefore both a debiasing technique and algorithms that exploit it in different problem settings. They suggest that the technique may help with related stochastic optimization challenges, presenting that broader use as a possibility rather than an established result.
neurips-2023-debiasing-conditional-stoch.tldr: Stochastic extrapolation reduces gradient bias in conditional stochastic optimization and enables improved sample-complexity bounds when combined with variance reduction.

paragraphs: Multi-agent reinforcement learning can achieve strong performance on individual tasks, yet retraining a system for every new task can be costly. This paper explores transferring knowledge through subtasks shared across tasks. The difficulty is making those subtasks genuinely independent of the source task, so that their usefulness survives a change in the overall problem.

DT2GS decomposes a task using a scalable subtask encoder and an adaptive subtask semantic module. The authors show that these components support two properties needed for task independence: avoiding overfitting to the source task and retaining consistent meanings that can scale across tasks. The decomposition is therefore intended to create reusable components with stable interpretations.

Empirical results show zero-shot generalization across tasks and transferability, along with better performance than existing methods on both single-task and multi-task problems. These findings support subtask decomposition as a route to reuse in multi-agent learning. The key idea is to shape both how subtasks are represented and how their meanings carry over, rather than assuming any decomposition will transfer.
neurips-2023-decompose-a-task-into-gener.tldr: DT2GS learns reusable subtasks with consistent, scalable meanings, improving multi-agent transfer and zero-shot generalization in empirical evaluations.

paragraphs: Discrete sampling is useful for simulation and optimization, and recent gradient-based methods can exploit accelerators such as GPUs. Comparing these methods remains difficult when papers use different experimental settings. Implementing samplers and target distributions also takes substantial effort, particularly when calibration and parallel execution must be handled consistently.

DISCS provides a shared software package and benchmark for three task families: sampling from classical graphical models, sampling from energy-based generative models, and sampling to solve combinatorial optimization problems. It supplies efficient implementations of representative existing samplers and a simple interface for adding new ones. This gives researchers a calibrated setting for direct comparisons.

The evaluations yield insights into scaling behavior, the design of proposal distributions, and adaptive sampling. The contribution is both practical infrastructure and evidence gathered through common evaluation procedures. By reducing implementation work and making experimental conditions more consistent, DISCS helps researchers assess sampling approaches across different tasks using a shared basis for comparison.
neurips-2023-discs-a-benchmark-for-discr.tldr: DISCS standardizes implementation and evaluation of discrete samplers across graphical models, generative models, and combinatorial optimization.

paragraphs: Energy-efficient scheduling controls how quickly a machine processes jobs, balancing power consumption with the quality of the resulting service. Predictions about future requests can improve these decisions, but their accuracy varies. The paper studies how scheduling algorithms can benefit from good predictions while retaining performance guarantees when predictions are poor.

The authors propose a flexible framework that accepts an offline algorithm and an online algorithm for the scheduling problem of interest. This makes the approach applicable to several energy-efficient scheduling objectives, including energy minimization with deadlines. The theoretical guarantee improves the competitive ratio when prediction error is small and keeps that ratio bounded regardless of prediction error.

The competitive ratio describes performance relative to an optimal schedule, so the results address both the value of accurate forecasts and resilience to inaccurate ones. Experiments on real and synthetic datasets also show improved performance. The contribution extends prediction-assisted scheduling beyond a single problem through a framework built from algorithms suited to the desired scheduling objective.
neurips-2023-energy-efficient-scheduling.tldr: A general scheduling framework gains stronger guarantees from accurate predictions while retaining bounded competitive performance for arbitrary prediction errors.

paragraphs: This paper establishes precise connections between changing the amount of training data and changing ridge regularization in ensemble ridge estimators. It studies combinations of regularization strength and subsample aspect ratio, where the latter is feature dimension divided by subsample size. Along particular paths through these combinations, certain properties of the resulting estimators become equivalent asymptotically.

The equivalences cover linear and quadratic functionals, yielding both structural and prediction-risk relationships. They require bounded moment assumptions on feature and response distributions while allowing arbitrary joint distributions. The authors also provide a data-dependent procedure for identifying the equivalent paths, connecting the mathematical relationships to information available from a dataset.

A consequence concerns optimally tuned ridge regression: its prediction risk is monotonic in the data aspect ratio under proportional asymptotics. This resolves the stated open problem for general data distributions subject to a mild regularity condition that maintains regression difficulty through linearized signal-to-noise ratios. The equivalences are asymptotic and path-specific, rather than claims that arbitrary finite-data subsampling and regularization choices are interchangeable.
neurips-2023-generalized-equivalences-be.tldr: The paper identifies asymptotic paths along which subsampling and ridge regularization have equivalent structural and risk properties.

paragraphs: Global routing in chip design must construct connected routes between pins. Generative models offer fast route generation, but disconnected outputs require repair using traditional methods and can erode that advantage. HubRouter addresses this problem by generating key routing points, called hubs, and then explicitly connecting those hubs with the pins.

The method has two phases. A condition-guided generative model produces hubs within a multi-task learning framework, with stripe mask learning addressing sensitivity to noisy points. An actor-critic model then performs the pin–hub connection through an RSMT construction module. This division lets learned generation propose useful route structure while a dedicated connection phase produces connected routes.

Experiments on simulated and real-world global routing benchmarks show improvements over state-of-the-art generative routing methods in wirelength, overflow, and running time. The paper also reports strengths in RSMT construction and interactive path replanning. These findings support separating key-point generation from route connection as an effective way to address a concrete weakness of generative routing.
neurips-2023-hubrouter-learning-global-r.tldr: HubRouter generates routing hubs and then connects them to pins, producing connected chip routes with improved benchmark efficiency and quality.

paragraphs: The paper proposes adapting weight decay during training instead of keeping its strength fixed. Weight decay discourages large model weights. Its strength determines how much this pressure influences training alongside the objective of correctly classifying examples. The proposed method automatically adjusts that strength at every training iteration.

For classification, the adjustment depends on the strength of updates associated with two objectives: cross-entropy, which measures classification error, and regularization based on the weights’ ℓ2 norm. This makes the regularization strength responsive to the updates occurring during training, rather than relying on a single setting chosen beforehand.

The authors report that this change can substantially improve adversarial robustness, in a setting where robust overfitting is a concern. Across multiple datasets and architectures, the improvements require no extra data. Compared with traditional weight decay using its best-tuned hyperparameters, they report relative robustness gains of 20% on CIFAR-100 and 10% on CIFAR-10. These are relative improvements, not percentage-point increases. The resulting models have robustness comparable to state-of-the-art methods.

The abstract also reports lower sensitivity to the learning rate and smaller weight norms. The authors connect those smaller norms with resistance to overfitting noisy labels and with robustness to pruning. Together, these findings suggest that adjusting regularization during training can benefit several aspects of model robustness.
neurips-2023-improving-robustness-with-a.tldr: Adaptive weight decay adjusts regularization at every training step and can improve adversarial robustness without extra data.

paragraphs: Stability-based generalization theory asks how much a learning algorithm changes when its training data changes. Randomized algorithms introduce a tension: averaging over internal randomness can yield favorable stability measures but only average guarantees, while conditioning on that randomness imposes a stronger requirement to obtain high-probability guarantees over both data and algorithm.

The paper introduces L2-uniform stability, which is uniform over data but measures algorithmic randomness through a second moment. Under this notion, the authors prove a strong exponential bound on the first moment of generalization error. They then use a bagging-based meta-algorithm within a confidence-boosting framework to obtain near-optimal generalization guarantees holding with high probability over both sources of randomness.

The theory is also applied to stochastic gradient descent for convex and nonconvex optimization with naturally decaying learning rates. It yields sharper exponential bounds than existing stability-based guarantees could establish in these settings. The advance is a new way to manage randomized stability, together with a confidence-boosting construction that converts the analysis into stronger probabilistic guarantees.
neurips-2023-l-2-uniform-stability-of-ra.tldr: L2-uniform stability enables sharper randomized-learning generalization bounds and, through bagging-based confidence boosting, near-optimal high-probability guarantees.

paragraphs: When several agents learn in different environments, sharing experience may help, but the usefulness of that experience depends on how similar their tasks are. This paper investigates that question for linear contextual bandits. The focus is on understanding when cooperative learning is beneficial despite differences among the environments in which agents make decisions.

The authors introduce H-LINUCB, a distributed algorithm based on the upper confidence bound approach. A central server coordinates the agents as they seek to minimize group regret, measuring the collective cost of learning through decisions. The formulation makes cooperation a group-level optimization problem while explicitly recognizing that agents need not face identical tasks.

The theoretical result assumes agents know the level of heterogeneity across environments. Under that assumption, H-LINUCB is provably optimal in regimes where tasks are highly similar or highly dissimilar. This characterizes performance at both ends of the similarity range; the stated result does not establish optimality for every intermediate level of heterogeneity or when heterogeneity is unknown.
neurips-2023-multi-agent-learning-with-h.tldr: H-LINUCB coordinates heterogeneous bandit learners and is provably optimal for highly similar or highly dissimilar tasks when heterogeneity is known.

paragraphs: Neural processes combine neural networks with stochastic processes to model flexible families of functions. They use context observations to shape those functions, allowing contextual knowledge to inform predictions. However, noisy context points can make the learned model sensitive: a small change in training data may produce a large model change and reduce generalization.

The paper brings algorithmic stability into neural processes to address this sensitivity. It provides theoretical guidance for obtaining stable solutions with strong generalization and describes an approach that can work with various neural process models. The analysis also supports a less biased approximation, connecting stability considerations with the quality of the model's approximation.

Experiments on synthetic and real-world data show improvements in accuracy and robustness. These results support treating sensitivity to training-data changes as a design concern for neural processes, alongside their ability to represent complex functions. The contribution combines theoretical guidance with empirical evidence that controlling this sensitivity can improve the reliability of predictions built from noisy context.
neurips-2023-neural-processes-with-stabi.tldr: The paper incorporates algorithmic stability into neural processes, providing theoretical guidance and empirical improvements in accuracy and robustness.

paragraphs: The paper develops a generative model inspired by the idea that stochastic neural responses represent samples from a posterior distribution. Its Hierarchical Exponential-family Energy-based model combines inference about observations with learning the distribution that generates them. This addresses both moment-to-moment interpretation and the ongoing adjustment of the model to its environment.

The method decomposes the partition function across layers and uses faster neurons to sample gradients of the resulting normalization terms. This permits partition-function estimation alongside inference and avoids the negative phase used in conventional energy-based models. The authors describe learning as local in both space and time, and show that neural adaptation can act as momentum to accelerate inference.

On natural images, the learned representations resemble those observed in biological vision. The model can also generate observations through either joint or marginal generation. Marginal generation performs better than joint generation in the reported comparison and matches other energy-based models. The results connect a biologically motivated account of inference with a functioning generative learning method.
neurips-2023-neural-sampling-in-hierarch.tldr: A hierarchical energy-based model supports simultaneous neural sampling and learning, with adaptation accelerating inference and marginal generation matching other EBMs.

paragraphs: Forecasting systems must handle multiple possible futures while respecting knowledge about the physical system. Deep learning models can struggle with either requirement: averaging possibilities can blur predictions, while unconstrained generation can produce implausible outcomes. PreDiff addresses both concerns through probabilistic forecasting combined with an explicit mechanism for incorporating domain knowledge.

The forecasting component is a conditional latent diffusion model. A knowledge-alignment mechanism estimates how far a prediction departs from imposed constraints at each denoising step, then adjusts the transition distribution accordingly. This makes constraints part of the generation process, allowing the model to account for uncertainty while steering its forecasts toward specified domain requirements.

The authors evaluate the approach on chaotic synthetic N-body MNIST data and real-world SEVIR precipitation data. They impose energy conservation for the synthetic system and anticipated precipitation intensity for SEVIR. Experiments support the method's ability to handle uncertainty, incorporate these forms of prior knowledge, and produce operationally useful forecasts. The evidence concerns these particular applications and constraints, without asserting universal physical correctness.
neurips-2023-prediff-precipitation-nowca.tldr: PreDiff combines probabilistic latent diffusion forecasting with stepwise knowledge alignment to incorporate physical constraints and precipitation-intensity guidance.

paragraphs: Multi-modal domain generalization asks models to work on unseen distributions while combining information from different modalities. The authors argue that forcing all modalities into a common embedding space can hinder this goal because modalities have distinct properties. SimMMDG addresses the issue by separating each modality's features into shared and modality-specific components.

The shared components are trained with supervised contrastive learning to capture joint properties. Distance constraints encourage diversity among the modality-specific features, preserving information that need not be shared. A cross-modal translation module further regularizes the representations and can also support generalization when a modality is missing. These components give shared information and distinctive information separate roles.

The paper provides theoretical support and reports strong multi-modal domain generalization results on EPIC-Kitchens and the newly introduced Human-Animal-Cartoon dataset. The findings support retaining modality-specific structure alongside aligned representations. The framework's contribution is a coordinated way to learn common properties without discarding distinctions among input types, while also providing a mechanism relevant to missing-modality settings.
neurips-2023-simmmdg-a-simple-and-effect.tldr: SimMMDG separates shared and modality-specific features to improve multi-modal generalization to unseen domains and support missing-modality scenarios.

paragraphs: A generated image can look convincing while failing to assign the requested attributes or relationships to the right objects. T2I-CompBench focuses on this compositional challenge. It provides 6,000 prompts spanning attribute binding, object relationships, and complex compositions, with finer divisions for color, shape, texture, spatial relationships, and non-spatial relationships.

The paper also introduces evaluation metrics designed specifically for compositional image generation. It investigates both the potential and limitations of multimodal language models as evaluators. These contributions address how to assess whether a scene follows the structure of a prompt, beyond the image's overall visual quality.

Alongside the benchmark, the authors propose GORS, which fine-tunes pretrained generators using reward-driven sample selection. Extensive evaluations benchmark previous methods and validate the proposed metrics and fine-tuning approach. The work therefore connects three parts of the same problem: prompts that expose composition errors, measurements suited to those errors, and a training approach intended to improve compositional ability.
neurips-2023-t2i-compbench-a-comprehensi.tldr: T2I-CompBench evaluates compositional image generation with 6,000 prompts and specialized metrics, while GORS uses reward-selected samples to improve pretrained generators.

paragraphs: No-regret learning has established guarantees for aggregate frequencies of play, but these do not fully explain how players' actual strategies evolve. This paper studies that day-to-day behavior in finite games with multiple players. It shifts attention from convergence to individual equilibria toward whether strategically meaningful sets of strategies remain stable and attract learning trajectories.

The relevant strategic property is closedness under better replies: leaving the set through a unilateral deviation imposes a cost on the deviating player. The authors prove an equivalence for products of pure-strategy sets. Such a product is closed under better replies if and only if its span is stable and attracting under regularized learning, directly linking strategic incentives to learning dynamics.

The paper also estimates convergence rates to these sets. Methods using entropic regularization, including exponential weights, converge geometrically, while projection-based methods reach them in finitely many iterations, even with bandit payoff feedback. These results characterize attraction to qualifying sets; they do not assert that every learning trajectory converges to a single equilibrium.
neurips-2023-the-equivalence-of-dynamic-.tldr: For products of pure-strategy sets, closedness under better replies is equivalent to stable, attracting spans under regularized learning, with method-dependent convergence rates.
